claim: §13.6 assumes bodha_msr_signals text 'cannot be shown to a reader' as-is and must be re-derived through a reader-facing vocabulary/register layer before serving to a layperson.
reality: Sampled 20 rows of bodha_msr_signals for chart_id 482012f1-710e-4a25-994a-93821f5871aa (LIMIT 20, no ORDER BY, effectively arrival order). 20/20 signal_headline_text and signal_summary_text values are raw deterministic key=value renders of internal config: category/key/value_num pairs, varga codes (D2/D6/D12/D20/D21), internal metric names (graha_yuddha_per_varga, house_bhava_bala_ratio, house_bhava_bala_subscore, graha_centrality:degree_centrality), and an internal methodological caveat string ('varga_assumption=physical_phenomenon_extended_to_mathematical_varga') baked into the summary text itself. None of the 20 are comprehensible to a layperson without translation; all require jyotish-technical background AND schema/internal-naming familiarity (e.g. 'bhava_adhipati_bala', 'value_num', bracketed source tag '[ga_structural]'). This is not merely 'technical register' — it is closer to a debug/audit log line than prose. The doc's own §16.6 table (line 2674) already independently reached the same verdict citing the same two columns and migration 325 — this sample corroborates it end-to-end against live data rather than schema comments.

recommended_action: §13.6's editorial obligation is real and correctly sized as unowned work, not an assumption to challenge. Do not downgrade the multi-week workstream estimate on the theory that some signals might already be 'close enough' — the sample (and the full 49,705-row population for this one chart, dominated by the same handful of key=value signal_type_id templates) shows uniform internal register with zero readable rows in a 20-row unweighted sample.

claim: Implicit sizing assumption: since signal text is machine-generated from a template per signal_type_id, the editorial fix is a small number of templates, not per-row hand-editing.
reality: GROUP BY signal_type_id on the full 49,705-row population for this chart shows heavy concentration in a handful of types (karaka_bhava_concordance:concordance_value = 4350 rows, bhava_significance_link:lord_aspects = 3480, convergence_count:total_edges = 2344, net_argala_per_varga:net_argala = 1740, lord_in_house_per_varga:lord_placement = 1740, bhava_significance_link:lord_placed = 1740, dispositor_chain_per_varga:chain = 1305, graha_centrality:degree_centrality = 1248, vargottama_per_varga:is_vargottama = 1232, dispositor_tree:tree_position = 1132 — top 10 types alone cover >21,000 rows). This is good news for scoping the fix: a per-signal_type_id NL rendering template (not per-row authoring) could plausibly cover the bulk of the corpus. This partially offsets the 'multi-week workstream' framing IF the fix is templated; it does NOT offset it if each signal_type_id's template needs jyotish-domain-accurate plain-language phrasing reviewed at acharya-grade (§J), which is still real editorial work across what is likely 50-150+ distinct signal_type_id values chart-wide.

claim: §19 P5' (and the architecture's implicit plan for citation-frequency-driven prioritization) assumes a queryable citation/message_parts linkage exists that can rank signal_ids by how often they are cited in existing conversations, producing a top-50 priority list for editorial rework.
reality: No message_parts table exists. conversation_messages stores citations (if any) inline in a parts_json JSONB blob, not as structured child rows — this matches the architecture doc's own §16.6 finding that 'message_parts child rows' (A-08) replacing the parts_json blob is itself still-pending target-architecture work, not built yet. A full-table ILIKE scan of conversation_messages.parts_json for 'signal_id', '"kind":"signal"', and 'bodha_msr_signals' returned 0 matching rows out of the whole table. Either (a) no conversation has ever cited an MSR signal by id, or (b) citations are recorded in a different, non-obvious shape this scan didn't match. Cannot distinguish between these from the DB alone without app-code inspection (out of scope for this read-only DB/MCP lane).
recommended_action: A top-50-by-citation-frequency priority list cannot be produced today — there is no data to rank. Either (1) confirm via code review (not DB) that citations of MSR signals have literally never occurred in production traffic, in which case §19 P5' needs a different prioritization heuristic (e.g. by signal_type_id row volume, as in PG1-S1-0002, or by domain-relevance to active predictions), or (2) if citations exist in some other jsonb shape, a lane with app-code access should locate and re-query it before P5' is scheduled.

claim: A-30 (§14.6): 'Calibration is gated on minimum-n, pooled across charts by default, reported as intervals, behind an explicit collect-only phase.'
reality: A-30 is a forward-looking design decision for the calibration/serving loop-back (mimamsa_calibration_get, minimum-n gating), not a claim about the current state of bodha_msr_signals editorial readability — it is orthogonal to this lane's S-1 charge (signal editorial sizing). The document itself (line 2905, 3060) already states the n=7 Brier precision-theater problem is real and unaddressed, and frames A-30 as the fix, not yet implemented. This lane's DB access (bodha_msr_signals, mimamsa_calibration_get) was not used to verify calibration-loop mechanics since that is a distinct workstream from signal-text readability; treating A-30 as in-scope for this lane risks scope creep past the charge. No DB evidence was gathered for or against A-30's implementation status.
recommended_action: A-30 should be verified by a lane scoped to the calibration/mimamsa serving path (mimamsa_calibration_get, mimamsa_outcome_record), not S-1. Recommend a follow-up PG-1 lane explicitly targeting §14.6/§14.7/§14A calibration-and-durability assumptions; do not fold that verdict into this signal-editorial-sizing report.

reality: Same scoping issue as A-30 (PG1-S1-0004): A-32 concerns disagreement/correction capture (a conversational-feedback and retrieval-behavior design decision), not signal-text editorial readability. The architecture doc's own §16.6 already independently marks 'Disagreement / correction capture' as ABSENT (worse: stubbed) in the current build (F-25c: 'the feedback UI silently discards'). recommended_action: Route A-32 verification to a lane scoped to conversational feedback/dispute-capture mechanics, inspecting the feedback endpoint and metadata_json shape in conversation_messages, not the S-1 signal-editorial lane.
